issues.description: Normalization only handles ClassName; ID, attribute, and type selectors with equivalent escapes will still false-negative
issues.detail: The invariant we want is: two selector strings that denote the same selector after CSS-escape decoding should compare equal after normalization. The implementation only triggers the getter/setter normalization for `parser.isClassName(node)`. The same escape ambiguity exists for IDs (`#u-m\00002b` vs `#u-m\+`), attribute selectors (`[data-x="\+"]`), tag selectors, and pseudo arguments. The fix as written is correct for the reported bug but the algorithm does not cover the stated invariant; a follow-up bug for `#id\+` is almost guaranteed.

issues.description: `node.value = node.value` relies on an undocumented side effect of postcss-selector-parser and warrants a stronger literate comment
issues.detail: The mechanism — getter returns unescaped, setter re-escapes canonically, and self-assignment therefore canonicalizes — is clever and correct, but it is exactly the sort of code Knuth warns about: correct, terse, and unreadable to a careful person who has not clicked the linked source. The comment is good; consider also recording (a) what canonical form the setter chooses (character-escape vs hex), (b) why the `raws.value` guard is a performance optimization rather than a correctness requirement, and (c) the postcss-selector-parser version this behavior was verified against. This protects against silent upstream regressions.

issues.description: `raws.value` guard couples correctness to an internal field; state the invariant it preserves
issues.detail: The early return `if (!node.raws?.value) return;` is labeled as a performance benefit, but it is also load-bearing for correctness reasoning: the claim is that when `raws.value` is absent, `node.value` is already in canonical form, so self-assignment is a no-op. That claim should be stated as an explicit invariant in the comment, because if upstream ever populates `node.value` without `raws.value` in a non-canonical form, this guard silently breaks normalization. A test that constructs both shapes and asserts canonical equality would pin the invariant.

issues.description: Test coverage proves the case but not the equivalence class
issues.detail: Two reject cases (`\00002b` vs `\+`, and `\2b` vs `\00002b`) are good, but the underlying claim is that all escape representations of the same codepoint collapse to one canonical form. Consider adding: uppercase vs lowercase hex (`\2B` vs `\2b`), hex with trailing space terminator (`\2b ` vs `\2b`), a non-ASCII codepoint, and a negative test confirming `.u-m\+` and `.u-n\+` remain distinct. This is the Knuth move: prove the equivalence class, not just two members of it.

issues.description: Walk now does two passes of work per node; trivially fine but worth naming
issues.detail: Complexity is unchanged asymptotically — still O(n) over selector nodes — and the added work per node is a cheap type check plus, for ClassName nodes with raws, a re-escape. On realistic stylesheets this is invisible. Noting it only because the PR description doesn't, and an honest complexity statement is part of the review.

review.summary: The fix is correct for the reported bug and uses a tidy, almost elegant mechanism — postcss-selector-parser's setter canonicalizes escaping, so `node.value = node.value` is a one-line normalizer. UNDER-AUDITED, however, on the stated invariant: the same escape ambiguity exists for ID, attribute, tag, and pseudo-argument selectors, and the patch only handles ClassName. The mechanism is also NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT: the self-assignment is load-bearing on undocumented upstream behavior and on the `raws.value` guard, and a careful reader deserves the invariant spelled out plus the parser version pinned. Tests demonstrate two members of the equivalence class but not the class; add uppercase-hex, space-terminated, and non-ASCII cases, plus a negative test. Asymptotically the walk is unchanged; no premature-optimization concerns.
